title: Transition, Operate, Deliver and Support

header.html: The ITIL Product and Service Lifecycle (10%)

Know the purpose of transition, operate, deliver and support; define release, continuous delivery, continuous deployment, incident, event, reliability, SRE, observability, service request, disaster, problem, error and known error; distinguish problem, error and known error
the official ITIL Foundation (Version 5) syllabus, version 5.0 (February 2026), categories 3.2.5 to 3.2.8 and 4.4.3 to 4.4.11

html:
1Transition

Purpose: move a new or changed product or service safely into live use with as little disruption as possible. [Verify live]

Term Meaning
Release A version of a product, service or component made available for use
Continuous delivery Every change is kept ready to release; the release itself is a decision (often manual)
Continuous deployment Every change that passes the tests is released to live automatically
Exam tip

. Delivery = ready to release, a person presses go. Deployment = released automatically. The extra word "deployment" means no human gate.

2Operate

Purpose: run the product so it performs as agreed, and handle incidents and events as they happen.

Term Meaning
Event Any change of state that has significance for managing a product or service
Incident An unplanned interruption or reduction in quality of a service
Reliability The ability to perform as intended and consistently
Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) Applying software engineering to operations to make systems more reliable
Observability Being able to understand a system's internal state from its outputs (logs, metrics, traces)
Exam tip

. Event = something happened (may be fine). Incident = something broke or got worse.

3Deliver

Purpose: provide the services to consumers as agreed and respond to their requests.

Term Meaning
Service request A request from a user for something that is part of normal service delivery, such as access or information

A service request is not an incident: nothing is broken.

4Support

Purpose: restore normal operation when something goes wrong, help users, and feed what is learned back into the product and service.

Term Meaning
Disaster A sudden, unplanned event that causes great damage or loss and stops critical work
Problem A cause or potential cause of one or more incidents
Error A flaw or malfunction in a component that can cause incidents
Known error A problem that has been analyzed but not yet resolved, usually with a workaround
Workaround A solution that reduces or removes the impact without fixing the cause

Exam tip

. Incident = the interruption. Problem = the cause under investigation. Error = the fault. Known error = the problem is understood, not yet fixed, workaround exists. [Verify live]

5All eight at a glance

Activity Purpose in a phrase
Transition go live safely
Operate run as agreed
Deliver provide the service
Support restore and help

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A team releases every change that passes automated tests directly to live without human approval. Which practice is this?

  • AContinuous integration
  • BContinuous delivery
  • CObservability
  • DContinuous deployment
Show the answer

Answer: D. Automatic release to live is continuous deployment.

S2A payment service is unavailable for 20 minutes. What is this?

  • AAn incident
  • BA service request
  • CA product prototype
  • DA value stream
Show the answer

Answer: A. An unplanned interruption of a service is an incident.

S3Which statement is CORRECT? (1) A known error is a problem that has been analyzed but not resolved. (2) A service request is the same as an incident. (3) A workaround reduces or removes the impact without fixing the cause. (4) An event always means something has failed.

  • A2 and 4
  • B1 and 4
  • C1 and 3
  • D2 and 3
Show the answer

Answer: C. Known errors and workarounds are defined that way.

S4Identify the missing word(s). [ ? ] is the ability to understand a system's internal state from its outputs.

  • AReliability
  • BObservability
  • CA release
  • DA disaster
Show the answer

Answer: B. That is observability.

S5A user asks for access to a shared drive. Which term describes the request?

  • AIncident
  • BProblem
  • CService request
  • DError
Show the answer

Answer: C. It is a normal request, not a failure.

S6The cause of repeated outages has been found, no fix exists yet, and the team uses a documented workaround. What is this?

  • AA known error
  • BA new incident
  • CA product specification
  • DA release
Show the answer

Answer: A. The problem is understood but not resolved, and a workaround exists.

S7Which activity has the purpose of moving a new or changed product safely into live use?

  • AAcquire
  • BOperate
  • CDiscover
  • DTransition
Show the answer

Answer: D. That is the purpose of transition.

6.2 Recall questions

R1Define an incident.

Show the answer

An unplanned interruption or reduction in the quality of a service.

R2Define an event.

Show the answer

Any change of state that has significance for managing a product or service.

R3What is the difference between continuous delivery and continuous deployment?

Show the answer

Delivery keeps every change ready to release; deployment releases every passing change automatically.

R4Define a problem.

Show the answer

A cause or potential cause of one or more incidents.

R5What is a known error?

Show the answer

A problem that has been analyzed but not resolved, usually with a workaround.

R6What does SRE stand for?

Show the answer

Site Reliability Engineering.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Transition / operate / deliver / support go live / run / provide / restore and help
Release a version made available for use
CD delivery = ready; deployment = automatic
Event / incident change of state / unplanned interruption
Problem / error / known error cause / fault / analyzed, unresolved, workaround
Service request normal request, nothing broken
